messages:
Anika: FYI support escalation from Acme Corp — p99 for /v1/generate jumped from ~300ms to ~1.2s around 08:05 UTC. They're seeing timeouts at the edge. Can SRE triage?
Kevin: grabbing traces now. Do we have a recent config push for continuous-batcher?
Maya: I see a config change rolled 08:02 that increased continuous_batcher.timeout_ms from 12 -> 40 and max_batch_size from 16 -> 64 (targeted perf experiment).
Liam: that explains tail. Larger max_batch_size + bigger timeout = increased head-of-line waiting for slow arrivals. p95 stable, p99 exploded.
Anika: we need a mitigation ASAP — customer is about to open a ticket. Can we rollback or patch?
Kevin: oncall can flip a runtime flag to lower timeout quickly. Suggest set timeout_ms back to 12 and cap max_batch_size to 32 as a compromise.
Maya: reproducer I ran against canary: run load with bursty arrival pattern (we use wrk2 script). Example:
```
wrk -t8 -c200 -d60s --script bursty.lua http://canary-infer:8080/v1/generate
```
In the trace you can see batching_wait spans at ~35ms per request ballooning when arrivals are bursty.
Liam: Dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood/s/dash?panel=batcher_wait_time shows 99th percentile spike exactly at 08:05. Also lng:request_latency by model.
support-bot: Incident created INC-2026, assigned to @Kevin and @Maya.
deploy-bot: Rolling config cdn-batch-experiment -> promoted to production at 08:01 by qa-team (change-id: 9876).
Kevin: quick mitigation: patch runtime via kong route override. Command I used in canary (will do prod if green):
```
curl -X POST "https://ops-api/redwood/runtime/flags" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ****' \
  -d '{"continuous_batcher.timeout_ms": 12, "continuous_batcher.max_batch_size": 32}'
```
Maya: applied on canary, running smoke. p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 330ms within two minutes.
Liam: runbook note: continuous-batcher experiments must be gated by tail-latency synthetic tests (bursty arrival) and a preflight traffic shape. I'll add a Grafana alert on batcher_wait_time_p99 > 500ms.
Anika: good. Can we schedule rollback of the prod experiment while we do a proper A/B?
Kevin: I scheduled a rollback job at 09:10 UTC to flip flag in prod if not addressed. For immediate safety I pushed the runtime override to prod at 08:26 — monitoring closely.
Maya: root cause summary: perf experiment increased buffering margin and batch size without verifying bursty arrival workloads. Continuous batching waits longer to fill batches; under bursty inter-arrival times that increases tail due to long-waited early requests. Also observed interaction with prefix cache miss causing KV lookups to add variance.
Liam: follow-ups: 1) revert experiment (done) 2) add canary load shape test 3) add preflight integration test and alert 4) update dev docs that changing timeout_ms must include p99 runbook signoff.
Anika: Customer update: told Acme we rolled back an experiment and reduced tail — asked to monitor. They want a postmortem.
Kevin: adding a short postmortem doc, will include repro steps, metrics, links, and the exact config diff.
Maya: config diff (what was rolled):
```
- continuous_batcher.timeout_ms: 12
- continuous_batcher.max_batch_size: 16
+ continuous_batcher.timeout_ms: 40
+ continuous_batcher.max_batch_size: 64
```
Liam: repro steps to include in PM: curl load script + wrk scripts, and the exact pattern (50ms bursts, random jitter). Also include a small script to simulate prefix-cache miss: set header `X-Bypass-Cache: true`.
Anika: Suggested interim policy: any change that increases timeout_ms by >10ms or max_batch_size by >2x must run p99 synthetic test with bursty workload before prod.
Kevin: agreed. I'll add it to the release checklist.
Maya: final status: prod override in place, p99 downgraded to acceptable range, monitoring shows stabilizing. I'll close the incident after postmortem is published.
support-bot: INC-2026 status -> resolved (monitoring).
Anika: thanks team. Please drop the postmortem link here when ready.
Kevin: PM draft: https://docs.redwood/postmortems/2109876543-continuous-batch-experiment — will publish after review.
Liam: adding notes to the devex doc about batching tradeoffs and a snippet for safe config: 
```
# safe defaults
continuous_batcher:
  timeout_ms: 12
  max_batch_size: 32
  enable_burst_protection: true
```
Maya: ACK, will review.
Anika: closing thread — good job on fast rollback and clear repro.
